name: Bow echo (warm season)
description: High instability + concentrated low-level shear + a moist (not too dry, not too wet) mid-troposphere — Johns/Hirt-style warm-season bow echo pattern, often along a quasi-stationary low-level thermal boundary. WFO Louisville tip sheet (Bow Echoes - warm season): 0-2.5 km shear 35-50 kt, 700-500 mb mean RH 50-80 %, CAPE often near 4500 J/kg. 0-3 km shear is used here as the 0-2.5 km proxy. Distinct from the existing derecho preset, which emphasizes stronger flow aloft. Starting point — tune across cycles.
